The action plan includes fostering human capital development, supporting job placement, raising SME competitiveness, pursuing service innovation through IT reform, and expanding the growth frontier by reforming the university system and promoting investment diversification.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Comprehensive productivity-focused programme combining human capital development, service sector innovation, and university system reform to raise economy-wide productivity and innovation capacity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The programme was 'presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007' with explicit goals and action plan components.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: A major, economy-wide productivity enhancement programme with explicit 50% growth target over five years, spanning human capital, service innovation, university reform, and SME competitiveness. Represents structural ambition to reshape innovation and productivity across multiple sectors and institutions.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007. Its goal is to boost productivity growth, as measured by value-added per worker, by 50% for all industries over five years.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: While it mentions fostering human capital and service innovation, the primary focus is on productivity growth across all industries rather than specific R&D funding or innovation instruments.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The 'SME Productivity Improvement Project' was included in 'Basic Policies 2007', aiming to enhance productivity of SMEs through IT utilization, corporate revitalization, and promotion of business start-ups. Major policy tools include providing financial support, R&D assistance, and developing human resources.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The R&D incentive for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was extended for an additional two years, promoting innovation and investment in research activities. Additionally, a permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy for R&D was estimated to raise the level of R&D spending by over 8%, alongside new measures including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure to support technological advancement.
